brief: There has been a BANDSTAND on the far bank since before the loop began and nothing has ever happened in it. The whole east side of the map has no gathering of any kind — every crowd this town has is transient, people passing through or claiming one seat each. Put something on in the bandstand on a summer afternoon and let people come and stand for it: an audience that arrives, holds still together, and thins when it ends. The green should be busy in July and empty in February.
successLooksLike: Across a folded multi-year probe, a summer afternoon puts a legible standing group at the bandstand and midwinter puts none; the audience arrives over minutes rather than appearing, reads as separate people rather than one shape at every moment it is on screen, and packs away when the thing ends without anybody teleporting. A filmstrip of the far bank shows no POP at set-up or strike.
avoid: Do not widen an existing spawn band to feed it — the east half already shares one budget, and the rate-of-zero law says give it its own arrival source. Do not stage it as timed steps; marketRaise is the pattern, N clamps on one 0..1 progress, so it packs away in reverse for free. And do not trust the 0.9-cell separation to hold by itself: cue c49 says that guarantee is at SPAWN only, and an audience STANDS STILL — which is the case the birds already fail.
